brickwork.title: Residential Building
brickwork.intro1: This residential brickwork project in Merseyside focused on strong, clean masonry that ties in with the existing property. From the first site visit, we planned the work around safe access, weather protection, and keeping disruption to a minimum for the homeowner.
brickwork.intro2: Our team carried out the brickwork in stages so each section could be checked, protected, and finished properly before moving on. Mortar mixes, coursing, and detailing were all matched to the surrounding build so the new work looks like it has always been part of the home.
brickwork.midText: The client wanted a durable finish that would stand up to everyday use and local weather without needing constant upkeep. We kept the site tidy throughout, communicated progress clearly, and made sure every elevation was left neat, square, and ready for the next stage of the build.
brickwork.tipsText: Good brickwork starts with solid preparation. Taking time to set out lines, protect existing surfaces, and plan deliveries makes a big difference to the finish and keeps the job running smoothly on site.
tips: Match brick type and mortar colour to existing work before work begins.
Keep materials covered and protected from rain during the build.
Check levels and coursing regularly as the wall rises.
Plan scaffold and access so work can continue safely.
Leave the site clean at the end of each day.
brickwork.overview: The main challenge was blending new brickwork with the current structure while working in a lived-in residential setting. We solved this with careful setting out, consistent workmanship, and clear communication so the client always knew what was happening next. The result is a solid, tidy finish the homeowner was happy to recommend.
brickwork.seoTitle: Residential Building (Brickwork) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
brickwork.metaDescription: Residential brickwork in Merseyside: new masonry matched to the existing house, built in stages with clean coursing and a tidy finish.

roof-lantern.title: Roof Lantern
roof-lantern.intro1: This roof lantern installation was designed to bring more natural light into the room below and give the space a brighter, more open feel. We worked to the client's layout and finish requirements, making sure the lantern suited both the roof structure and the look of the property.
roof-lantern.intro2: The installation included careful measuring, structural checks, and weatherproof detailing so the lantern would perform properly in all seasons. Our team fitted the unit with precision and sealed the surrounding area to protect against water ingress.
roof-lantern.midText: Natural light makes a huge difference to how a room feels, but the fitting has to be done right. We focused on clean lines, secure fixings, and a finish that looks sharp inside and out, with minimal disruption while the work was carried out.
roof-lantern.tipsText: A roof lantern needs to be planned as part of the whole roof, not just dropped in at the end. Getting the opening, supports, and weathering details right early saves time and avoids problems later.
tips: Confirm roof structure and load before cutting the opening.
Choose a lantern size that suits the room below.
Use quality flashings and sealants for long-term weather protection.
Check internal finishes early so plasterwork and trims line up.
Test for leaks before signing off the installation.
roof-lantern.overview: The challenge here was fitting a modern lantern into an existing roof without compromising weather protection or the internal finish. We managed this with accurate setting out, careful installation, and attention to detail on all sealing points. The client was left with a bright, practical feature that looks great from inside and out.
roof-lantern.seoTitle: Roof Lantern (Architecture) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
roof-lantern.metaDescription: Roof lantern installation in Merseyside, bringing natural light into the room below with weatherproof detailing and a clean internal finish.

bespoke-joinery.title: Panelled Sink Unit
bespoke-joinery.intro1: This bespoke joinery project was a custom panelled sink unit built to fit the room and fixed securely to the wall. Rather than a standard off-the-shelf vanity, we made a unit that suited the space, plumbing layout, and finish the client wanted.
bespoke-joinery.intro2: Our joiners planned the panelling, carcass, and fixings so the unit sat flush to the wall with clean lines and a solid, built-in look. Every detail was measured on site to make sure the sink area worked practically and looked right in the room.
bespoke-joinery.midText: A wall-connected sink unit needs to be level, secure, and finished properly around pipes and fittings. We took care with the panel detail, edges, and seal lines so the unit feels like part of the room rather than something dropped in at the end.
bespoke-joinery.tipsText: A panelled sink unit works best when the wall fixing, plumbing positions, and finished sizes are planned early. That keeps the fit tight and avoids awkward gaps around the basin and worktop.
tips: Check wall structure and fixing points before building the unit.
Confirm sink and tap positions before final panel sizes are cut.
Allow access for plumbing maintenance behind or within the unit.
Use moisture-resistant materials in wet areas.
Protect walls and floors during fitting and finishing.
bespoke-joinery.overview: The challenge was building a panelled sink unit that connected neatly to the wall while housing the basin and plumbing cleanly. We solved this with accurate site measurements, secure wall fixings, and careful finishing on the panels. The client was left with a smart, custom unit that looks built in and works well every day.
bespoke-joinery.seoTitle: Panelled Sink Unit (Interior) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
bespoke-joinery.metaDescription: A bespoke panelled sink unit built and fitted to the wall in a Merseyside home, measured on site around the plumbing and basin.

panel-wall.title: Panel Wall
panel-wall.intro1: This panel wall project created a standout interior feature with a clean, modern finish. The aim was to add character to the room while keeping the installation neat, secure, and in proportion with the space.
panel-wall.intro2: We prepared the wall surface, set out the panel layout, and fitted each section with care so joints, lines, and edges all looked intentional. The result is a sharp feature wall that lifts the whole room.
panel-wall.midText: Feature walls work best when the detail is right. We focused on alignment, fixing, and finish quality so the panels sit flat, look balanced, and stand up to everyday use in a busy home.
panel-wall.tipsText: Panel walls need a flat, sound base and a clear layout before fixing begins. Spending time on preparation makes the finished wall look far more polished.
tips: Check walls are level and dry before installation.
Plan panel layout to avoid narrow cuts at edges.
Use the right fixings for the wall substrate.
Work from a central line to keep the pattern balanced.
Fill and touch up carefully for a seamless finish.
panel-wall.overview: The challenge was turning a plain wall into a feature without making the room feel busy. We solved this with careful layout, precise fitting, and a finish that suits the rest of the interior. The client was left with a modern panel wall that looks great and feels well built.
panel-wall.seoTitle: Panel Wall (Interior) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
panel-wall.metaDescription: A modern panelled feature wall fitted in a Merseyside home, with a careful layout, flat fixing and neat finishing on every edge.

interior-wall-tiling.title: Wall Tiling
interior-wall-tiling.intro1: This interior wall tiling project focused on a clean, durable finish that suits the room and stands up to everyday use. The layout was planned carefully so lines, joints, and edges all looked balanced and intentional.
interior-wall-tiling.intro2: We prepared the wall surfaces, set out the tile pattern, and fitted each section with precision. The result is a neat, professional tiled wall that lifts the space and feels built to last.
interior-wall-tiling.midText: Wall tiling works best when the preparation and setting out are right from the start. We focused on level surfaces, accurate cuts, and tidy finishing so the completed wall looks sharp and performs well over time.
interior-wall-tiling.tipsText: Good wall tiling starts with a sound, flat surface and a clear layout. Taking time on preparation keeps the finished wall looking neat and helps the tiles stay secure.
tips: Check walls are level, dry, and suitable for tiling.
Plan the tile layout before fixing begins.
Use the right adhesive and grout for the room conditions.
Keep grout lines consistent for a clean finish.
Protect surrounding surfaces during installation.
interior-wall-tiling.overview: The challenge was tiling an interior wall with a finish that looked sharp and suited the rest of the room. We solved this with careful surface preparation, accurate setting out, and neat detailing on every edge. The client was left with a smart tiled wall they were happy with.
interior-wall-tiling.seoTitle: Wall Tiling (Interior) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
interior-wall-tiling.metaDescription: Interior wall tiling in Merseyside, with proper surface preparation, accurate setting out and consistent grout lines.

plastering.title: Ready for Decoration
plastering.intro1: This plastering and door project covered smooth wall and ceiling finishes and a fire door fitted ready for decoration. We prepared each surface carefully so the plasterwork went on cleanly and the new door sat neatly in its frame.
plastering.intro2: Our team worked through the plastering in stages — protecting the rest of the property, keeping dust under control, and finishing joints, angles, and reveals neatly around the new door.
plastering.midText: Good plastering is about flat surfaces, clean corners, and details that look right once painted — especially around door frames and new openings. We left this room smooth, secure, and ready for the next stage of decoration.
plastering.tipsText: A finish ready for decoration starts with sound preparation — particularly where walls have been altered or a new door has been fitted. Getting backgrounds flat and dry before skimming saves time later and gives a much better result.
tips: Check walls and ceilings are dry and stable before plastering.
Plan door openings and frame sizes early in the project.
Protect floors, woodwork, and fittings from splashes and dust.
Finish corners and reveals neatly around the door frame.
Allow proper drying time before decoration begins.
plastering.overview: The challenge was combining a new door installation with plasterwork that would look flawless once decorated. We solved this with careful preparation and consistent finishing on every wall, ceiling, and frame detail. The client was left with a room ready to decorate.
plastering.seoTitle: Ready for Decoration (Plastering) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
plastering.metaDescription: Plastering and fire door installation in Merseyside, leaving smooth walls, ceilings and reveals ready for decoration.

wall-removal.title: New Door Opening
wall-removal.intro1: This wall removal project created a new opening between rooms, with the structural work planned and carried out safely from start to finish. We assessed the wall, installed temporary support, and removed the masonry in a controlled way to form the new doorway.
wall-removal.intro2: Our team worked in stages so the building stayed supported throughout, with dust sheets and protection in place for the rest of the property. Once the opening was formed, the area was left neat, secure, and ready for the next stage of the build.
wall-removal.midText: Removing a wall for a new door or passage needs proper planning — not just knocking through. We focused on safe support, clean removal, and a tidy finish so the opening was ready for framing, plastering, and the door to be fitted.
wall-removal.tipsText: Wall removal should always start with a clear understanding of what is structural and how the load will be supported. Getting props, lintels, and protection right keeps the job safe and avoids costly problems later.
tips: Confirm whether the wall is load-bearing before work begins.
Install temporary support and props where required.
Protect adjoining rooms from dust and debris.
Remove masonry in a controlled sequence.
Leave the opening clean and ready for the next trade.
wall-removal.overview: The challenge was forming a new doorway safely in a lived-in property without damaging surrounding finishes or compromising the structure. We solved this with careful support, staged removal, and clear communication throughout. The client was left with a secure opening ready for the follow-on work.
wall-removal.seoTitle: New Door Opening (Wall Removal) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
wall-removal.metaDescription: Wall removal in Merseyside to form a new door opening, with temporary support, controlled removal and a clean, secure finish.

flat-roof.title: Flat Roof Refurbishment
flat-roof.intro1: This flat roof had reached the end of its life, with a worn, patchy surface around the existing roof lantern. We re-covered the roof with new felt, finishing it neatly around the lantern, upstands and edges.
flat-roof.intro2: The work was planned around the lantern so it stayed sealed and watertight throughout. Each section of felt was laid and lapped in order, with the joints and edges finished so water runs off the roof properly.
flat-roof.midText: The before and after photos show the difference a new flat roof makes. The finished surface is clean, even and sealed, protecting the room below and giving the roof many more years of life.
flat-roof.tipsText: A flat roof often needs attention long before it starts to leak. Catching wear early and re-covering the roof properly is usually far cheaper than repairing water damage inside.
tips: Check flat roofs for cracking, blistering and standing water.
Pay close attention to edges, upstands and around rooflights.
Clear debris and moss so water can drain freely.
Re-cover the whole roof once patch repairs stop working.
Make sure rooflights and lanterns are properly sealed in.
flat-roof.overview: The challenge was renewing the roof covering while keeping the existing roof lantern sealed and protected. We worked carefully around it and finished every edge and joint neatly, leaving a clean, watertight flat roof.
flat-roof.seoTitle: Flat Roof Refurbishment (Roofing) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
flat-roof.metaDescription: Flat roof refurbishment in Merseyside: an old, worn roof re-covered with new felt and finished neatly around the existing roof lantern. Before and after photos.

french-doors.title: French Doors & Windows
french-doors.intro1: On this job the old windows came out and the brickwork was opened up so new French doors and windows could be fitted, giving the rooms behind direct access out to the garden.
french-doors.intro2: The new frames are finished in dark grey to suit the brickwork, with French doors in the centre and matching windows either side.
french-doors.midText: Opening up an existing wall needs careful planning and support, so the structure stays sound while the brickwork is altered. Once the openings were formed, the doors and windows were fitted and sealed in, ready for the outside to be finished.
french-doors.tipsText: Swapping windows for French doors can transform how a room is used, but the opening has to be planned properly. Getting the support, sizes and finishes right at the start avoids problems later.
tips: Plan any new or enlarged openings and their support before cutting into brickwork.
Measure openings accurately and order doors and windows in good time.
Choose frame colours that suit the brickwork and the rest of the building.
Make sure thresholds and sills are set so water runs away from the building.
Seal frames properly once fitted to keep out draughts and rain.
french-doors.overview: The challenge was altering the existing brickwork safely and fitting the new doors and windows neatly into the openings. The result is a much brighter space with easy access straight out onto the garden.
french-doors.seoTitle: French Doors & Windows in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
french-doors.metaDescription: French doors and windows fitted in Merseyside: old windows removed, brickwork opened up and new dark grey doors and windows installed.

paved-pathway.title: Paved Pathway
paved-pathway.intro1: This job was a new paved pathway running along the side of a building, giving tidy, level access to the doors along that side.
paved-pathway.intro2: Large paving slabs were laid along the length of the building, with an edging line along the garden side to give the path a clean finish.
paved-pathway.midText: A path right next to a building has to be laid carefully, with the levels set so rainwater runs away from the walls rather than towards them. The finished path gives a smart, hard-wearing route along the building.
paved-pathway.tipsText: Good paving is all about what is underneath. A properly prepared base and the right falls make the difference between a path that lasts and one that sinks or holds water.
tips: Dig out and prepare a firm, compacted base before laying slabs.
Set falls so water drains away from walls and doorways.
Keep paving below damp proof course level next to the building.
Use an edging along open sides to stop the path spreading.
Keep joints even and fill them properly once the slabs are down.
paved-pathway.overview: The challenge was laying a long, straight path tight to the building while keeping the levels right for drainage. The finished pathway is level, neat and ready for everyday use.
paved-pathway.seoTitle: Paved Pathway (Landscaping) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
paved-pathway.metaDescription: A new paved pathway laid along a building in Merseyside, with large slabs, a neat edging and levels set to drain water away from the walls.

stud-walls-panelling.title: Stud Walls & Panelling
stud-walls-panelling.intro1: These photos show examples of our interior work, from building new timber stud walls and blocking up old doorways to finishing rooms with slatted wood panelling.
stud-walls-panelling.intro2: Stud walls are framed out in timber and fixed securely so they are ready for boarding, and old doorways are framed and boarded in flush with the surrounding wall, ready for plastering.
stud-walls-panelling.midText: Slatted panelling adds warmth and character to a room, and it works best when the walls behind it are straight and solid. Whatever the job, getting the framing right first means the finished room looks sharp and lines up properly.
stud-walls-panelling.tipsText: Interior alterations like these are about solid framing and careful finishing. A straight, secure frame makes boarding, plastering and panelling far easier to get right.
tips: Build stud walls square, level and securely fixed top and bottom.
Plan cables and sockets before the walls are boarded.
Frame blocked-up doorways so the infill sits flush with the wall.
Leave infills ready for plaster so the join disappears once finished.
Fix panelling to a straight base so the slats line up neatly.
stud-walls-panelling.overview: Interior alterations like these need solid framing and careful finishing. From new walls and blocked-up doorways through to feature panelling, we make sure each stage is done properly so the finished room looks right and lasts.
stud-walls-panelling.seoTitle: Stud Walls & Panelling (Interior) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
stud-walls-panelling.metaDescription: Examples of interior work in Merseyside: new timber stud walls, old doorways blocked up ready for plaster, and slatted wood panelling.

strip-out.title: Strip-Out & Steel Beam
strip-out.intro1: This older property was stripped right back to the brick, removing tired plaster and finishes so the walls, ceilings and structure could be properly assessed and renovated.
strip-out.intro2: A steel beam supports an opening in the structure, and the walls were prepared with timber battens ready for the next stage.
strip-out.midText: Stripping a property back shows exactly what you are working with. It means any problems in the brickwork or structure can be dealt with properly before new finishes go on, instead of being covered up.
strip-out.tipsText: A full strip-out is often the best starting point for renovating an older home. Getting the structure right first makes everything that follows easier and longer lasting.
tips: Strip back to the brick to see the true condition of the walls.
Have structural changes such as steel beams properly planned and supported.
Deal with damp or damaged brickwork before new finishes go on.
Use battens to give a straight, even base for boarding.
Keep the property safe and secure while it is stripped out.
strip-out.overview: The challenge was taking an older property back to its shell safely and making sure the structure was properly supported for the renovation. With the strip-out done and the steel in place, the property was ready for the rebuild.
strip-out.seoTitle: Strip-Out & Steel Beam (Structural) in Merseyside | Cottle Construction
strip-out.metaDescription: Property strip-out in Merseyside: an older home stripped back to the brick, with a steel beam supporting an opening and walls battened ready for renovation.
